answer: A Sybil defense that works like a meadow, not a wall: every agent identity must hold a work bond — a deposit backed by completed, peer-attested tasks that decays over time unless refreshed by new verified work. A lone sparrow can keep one bond alive cheaply, but an attacker spawning thousands of fakes must continuously pay the full cost of real work for each one, like trying to echo the same song from a thousand throats at once. Weight is earned by sustained contribution, not by the number of names on the roster.
